title: Lower generic CIR scalar op spellings
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks cir.binop and cir.unary as P0 unsupported generic scalar spellings that can block ordinary C emitted by newer/different CIR producers.

What to do:
- Add parsing/lowering for cir.binop and cir.unary spellings.

- Add differential fixtures that force these spellings.

title: Lower low-level CIR branch variants
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks cir.brcond and cir.switch.flat as P0 unsupported control-flow variants. Slate supports structured branch/switch forms, but these lower-level forms can appear and should not block ordinary C.

What to do:
- Add parser and lowerer support for cir.brcond.
- Add parser and lowerer support for cir.switch.flat.
- Prefer structured Rust output when the CFG shape permits it; use conservative state-machine style only when needed.
- Add differential fixtures and update docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.
close_reason: cir.brcond/cir.switch.flat come only from --cir-flatten-cfg, which Slate never runs. Verified: if/else, ternary, &&, ||, for, while, do-while, switch, goto all stay structured through Slate's emit pipeline (0 brcond/switch.flat). Supporting them would be untestable dead code. Documented in docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.

title: Fix typed dispatch-loop break mismatch in generated libyaml output
description: cargo check of the generated ~/libyaml crate reports E0308 mismatched types for labeled dispatch-loop breaks such as break '__dispatch0; in contexts expecting i32. title: Lower CIR aggregate extract and insert member ops
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks cir.extract_member and cir.insert_member as P1 unsupported. Aggregate value mutation/extraction appears once structs/unions are manipulated by value rather than only through addresses.

What to do:
- Add parser/lowerer support for cir.extract_member and cir.insert_member.
- Preserve C aggregate semantics while generating Rust field/member updates compatible with existing struct representation.
- Add differential fixtures for struct value extraction, mutation, nested aggregates, and array-containing structs where supported.
- Update docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.

title: Lower CIR memory operation intrinsics
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks cir.libc.memchr, cir.libc.memcpy, cir.libc.memmove, cir.libc.memset, cir.memcpy_inline, and cir.memset_inline as P1 unsupported. Memory operations are high-leverage for real C and stdlib expansion.

What to do:
- Add parser/lowerer support for the CIR memory operation family.
- Map libc and inline forms to Rust/libc/std::ptr operations with correct overlap behavior for memmove versus memcpy.
- Add differential fixtures for scalar buffers, struct/array copies, memset zero/nonzero, memchr hits/misses, and overlapping memmove.
- Update docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.
close_reason: Lowered the cir.libc.mem* family (memcpy/memmove/memset/memchr) to byte-wise std::ptr ops + __slate_memchr helper; added PtrCopy/WriteBytes AST nodes and 4 differential fixtures. Plain libc mem* calls already worked via extern; only clang builtins/aggregate bit_cast raise these ops. Idiom-recognizer is a no-op stub upstream (noted in emit.rs).

title: Lower CIR bitfield get and set ops
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks cir.get_bitfield and cir.set_bitfield as P1 unsupported. C bitfields are common in systems headers and data layouts.

What to do:
- Add parser/lowerer support for cir.get_bitfield and cir.set_bitfield.
- Preserve signedness, width, offset, masking, and update semantics from CIR.
- Add differential fixtures for signed/unsigned bitfields, adjacent fields, boundary widths, and read-modify-write updates.
- Update docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.
close_reason: Lowered cir.get_bitfield/cir.set_bitfield as mask+sign-extend over per-field struct storage (behaviorally identical to CIR shared storage for well-defined C). Added bitfield_ops differential fixture (signed/unsigned, adjacent fields, boundary widths, read-modify-write, 40-bit long-long) and marked ops supported in docs. Verified: cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release (116 passed).

title: Lower CIR checked and overflowing arithmetic ops
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks cir.add.overflow, cir.sub.overflow, cir.mul.overflow, cir.div.overflow, cir.rem.overflow, and cir.binop.overflow as P1 unsupported. These can appear for overflow builtins and checked arithmetic code.

What to do:
- Add parser/lowerer support for the overflowing arithmetic op family.
- Map to Rust overflowing_* or equivalent tuple-result handling with C-compatible semantics.
- Add fixtures for each arithmetic family member, including signed and unsigned cases where applicable.
- Update docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.
close_reason: Duplicate of closed slate-2j6. This Clang's CIR dialect (CIROps.td, CIR_BinOpOverflow) only defines cir.add.overflow/cir.sub.overflow/cir.mul.overflow — no cir.div.overflow, cir.rem.overflow, or cir.binop.overflow (those are incubator-only, never emitted). All three real ops are lowered in src/lower.rs:928-930 to Rust overflowing_* tuple results and covered by tests/fixtures/overflow_scalar_ops.c (signed add/sub/mul, unsigned add, long-long mul).

title: Lower CIR atomics to real Rust atomics (AtomicN::from_ptr)
description: Replace the non-atomic RMW lowering of cir.atomic.* with genuine std::sync::atomic ops so the output is correct once multithreaded programs land. Use AtomicN::from_ptr(store_address(ptr)) to view the existing integer slot atomically without changing its storage. fetch->fetch_add/sub/and/or/xor/nand/max/min (recompute new value when fetch_first is absent); xchg->swap; cmpxchg->compare_exchange (strong, to stay deterministic); fence->std::sync::atomic::fence. Also route mem_order-carrying cir.load/cir.store to atomic load()/store() so a shared _Atomic object is never accessed non-atomically (else data race under threads). Float/pointer atomics keep the non-atomic fallback (no std atomic float).
design: atomic_wrapper(rust_ty)->Option<AtomicN name> for i8..u64/isize/usize/bool. Ordering from C mem_order enum (0 relaxed,1 consume,2 acquire,3 release,4 acqrel,5 seqcst); clamp to load/store-valid orderings; consume->Acquire; relaxed thread fence is a no-op (fence(Relaxed) panics in Rust). compare_exchange always strong (weak may spuriously fail and diverge from C in differential tests).
acceptance_criteria: tests/fixtures/atomics.c still passes generated_differential; generated Rust uses AtomicN::from_ptr(...).fetch_*/swap/compare_exchange and atomic load/store; no non-atomic access to _Atomic objects.
close_reason: Atomics now lower to real std::sync::atomic ops via AtomicN::from_ptr (fetch_*/swap/compare_exchange/fence + atomic load/store). atomics.c differential passes; pthread program lowers correct atomic ops. Merged to main.

title: Lower cir.atomic.cmpxchg (compare-exchange)

close_reason: Lowered as non-atomic RMW via store_address; atomics.c fixture passes generated_differential. Merged to main.

title: Lower cir.atomic.xchg (atomic exchange)

close_reason: Lowered as non-atomic RMW via store_address; atomics.c fixture passes generated_differential. Merged to main.

title: Lower cir.atomic.fetch (atomic RMW fetch ops)
description: Lower cir.atomic.fetch(ptr,val) to a non-atomic read-modify-write. binop attr selects the op (0=Add,1=Sub,2=And,3=Xor,4=Or,5=Nand,6=Max,7=Min); Nand => !(old & val); Max/Min => old.max/min(val). The fetch_first unit attr means the op returns the pre-op value (fetch_add); its absence means it returns the post-op value (add_fetch). Emit: read *store_address(ptr), compute new, write back, bind result to old or new.
acceptance_criteria: atomic_fetch_add/sub/and/or/xor and __atomic_add_fetch fixtures translate without warnings and pass differential.
close_reason: Lowered as non-atomic RMW via store_address; atomics.c fixture passes generated_differential. Merged to main.

title: Support CIR C atomics (cir.atomic.*)
description: C11/GNU atomics lower to distinct CIR ops that Slate currently drops (warns 'unsupported CIR op'): cir.atomic.fetch, cir.atomic.xchg, cir.atomic.cmpxchg, cir.atomic.fence. Atomic loads/stores already lower correctly (plain cir.load/cir.store carrying mem_order/sync_scope attrs, which are safely ignored). Because Slate's correctness bar is single-threaded differential testing, lower these as plain non-atomic read-modify-write through store_address(ptr) (transliterate-first); real Rust atomics are a later idiomatization fixup.
design: Use store_address(ptr) to obtain a uniform *mut T for slot/global/member/element/raw-ptr, then RMW inside unsafe. binop enum: 0=Add,1=Sub,2=And,3=Xor,4=Or,5=Nand,6=Max,7=Min. fetch_first attr present => op returns old value; absent => returns new value.

title: Lower calls to external libc functions via extern "C" declarations
description: Slate emits bare Rust calls to external C symbols (e.g. puts(...), strcpy(...), sqrt(...), malloc(...)) with no declaration, so the generated Rust fails to compile (cannot find function). Fix: for any called function with no body in the translation unit, emit an extern "C" { fn name(args) -> ret; } declaration (or route to libc::) so the call links against the system C library. Covers stdlib_coverage probes: stdio/{puts,putchar,fputs,fprintf,sprintf,snprintf}, string/*, stdlib/{atoi,atol,labs,strtol,malloc_free,calloc,qsort}, math/*, ctype/* (via __ctype_b_loc/__ctype_toupper_loc).

close_reason: Collect body-less cir.func decls into an 'unsafe extern "C"{}' block; extern call sites wrap in unsafe and 'as'-cast fixed args to declared param types (variadic '...' preserved). Also: string literals render *mut (weaken to *const for printf), #cir.ptr<null> -> null_mut(), added cir.ptr_diff (offset_from), and -lm in the C harness. stdlib_coverage 25->40 passing: acceptance probes puts/strcpy/strlen/sqrt/atoi/malloc_free all pass, plus ctype/* (via __ctype_b_loc), libm sqrt/sin/cos/exp/log/pow/fmod, string mem*/str* (chr/rchr/str/cmp/ncmp), atol/calloc/strtol, snprintf/sprintf/putchar. title: Refactor fuzz generator into C-subset program generator
description: The current BNF expander mostly stitches fixed template fragments together, so generated programs do not exercise variable scope, expression composition, reusable declarations, or realistic statement interactions. Refactor fuzzing around a C-aware program generator that can consume a grammar/BNF for the supported syntax but also maintain generation state: declared variables, types, scopes, functions, globals, and expression contexts. The generator should produce valid C programs for Slate's supported subset, with variables that can be declared, assigned, read, passed to functions, used in array indices, struct/union fields, loops, sizeof, volatile/static contexts where supported, and combined into expressions/statements without violating C validity. The design should be closer to a small csmith-style generator for our subset than a pure random text expander. It should keep deterministic seeds, shrinking/debuggability where practical, and integrate with the existing differential test harness and BNF fuzz entry point. Acceptance criteria: design is documented; generator can emit multi-function programs with scoped variables and expressions; generated programs compile as C and translate with Slate; differential tests run multiple seeds; existing simple BNF tests are either preserved as smoke tests or migrated cleanly.
notes: Refactoring tests/bnf_fuzz.rs fuzzing around a stateful C-subset generator (tests/support/cgen.rs). Keeps BNF grammar+expander as a smoke test; new generator_differential runs multiple seeds. Value-bound tracking guarantees no i32 overflow / OOB so C==Rust.
close_reason: Refactored fuzzing around a stateful C-subset generator (tests/support/cgen.rs): scope/type env + function-signature state compose multi-function programs with scoped vars, expressions, calls; value-bound tracking guarantees no UB so C==Rust. BNF expander kept as bnf_expander_smoke; generator_differential runs N seeds (40 verified green). Design in docs/fuzzing.md. All tests + fmt pass.

title: Rewrite string length/compare: strlen/strcmp/strncmp/memcmp
description:
Once a value is lifted to &str/&[u8]/String (slate-58r.1), rewrite:
- strlen(s) -> s.len()
- strcmp(a,b) == 0 -> a == b ; strcmp ordering -> a.cmp(b)
- strncmp(a,b,n) -> a[..n] compare (bounds-checked)
- memcmp(a,b,n) on lifted slices -> a == b (also usable via slate-58r.2)

Most common and most mechanical family -> highest priority. Keep raw libc call when operands are not lifted.
acceptance_criteria: - Lifted-operand calls render as len()/==/cmp/slice-compare; unlifted operands stay raw.\n- strcmp sign semantics preserved (==0 vs <0/>0 mapped to == / Ordering).\n- Differential fixtures cover equal, prefix, and ordering cases.
close_reason: Adjusted lifted strlen rewrites to keep Rust's native usize result: generated temps now use usize and assign s.len() directly instead of u64 plus as u64. Verified fixture output plus cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Substrate: lift char* / nul-terminated buffers to &str / String / &[u8]
description:
Analysis + lowering pass that recognizes when a C `char*` / `const char*` (and char-array locals) can be represented as a Rust `&str`, `String`, or `&[u8]` carrying an explicit length, instead of a bare `*const i8`/`*mut i8`.

This is THE highest-leverage prerequisite: it unlocks the entire str* / parse family (slen/compare/copy/search/parse rewrites). None of those can be done safely until a value is lifted, because a raw `*const i8` has no length and no UTF-8/nul guarantee.

Must preserve C semantics precisely: nul-termination boundary, non-UTF-8 bytes (prefer `&[u8]`/`CStr` when bytes aren't provably UTF-8), aliasing/mutation through the pointer, and pointer identity where later code does arithmetic on it. Where a value cannot be proven liftable, leave it as the raw pointer (correctness over idiom).

## Context
Gates slate-58r string-family rewrites. Broader than libc: also affects string-literal and char-array representation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Lowered code represents provably-liftable C strings as &str/String/&[u8] with a length, not raw *const i8.
- Non-UTF-8 / byte-buffer cases fall back to &[u8]/CStr, never lossy String.
- Values used in raw pointer arithmetic or passed to unlifted externs stay raw.
- Differential tests green; fixtures cover UTF-8, embedded-non-ASCII, and mutation-through-pointer cases.
close_reason: Implemented AST string_lift fixup with structural &str/&[u8] Rust AST types, conservative raw-pointer safety checks, and differential coverage. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Idiomatize libc calls into higher-level Rust forms
description:
Why: Slate currently lowers most C standard-library calls faithfully but unidiomatically -- they flow through the generic extern path (declared `unsafe extern "C"`, called through raw pointers / `libc`). Only the mem* family has dedicated handlers (src/lower.rs:1183). memchr (slate-04q.26) and printf->format-macro (slate-04q.8) are the only idiomatization tickets so far. This epic collects the rest.

Key architectural insight: the function-call rewrite is the EASY half. The hard, high-leverage prerequisite is a set of DATA-TYPE LIFTING passes that turn raw C representations into owned/borrowed Rust types carrying length and provenance:
- `char*` / nul-terminated buffers -> `&str` / `String` / `&[u8]`
- `(T*, len)` pairs -> `&[T]` / `Vec<T>`
- heap and resource handles (`malloc`/`free`, `FILE*`) -> `Box`/`Vec` / `std::fs`+`io`

Almost every str*/parse/sort/heap/stdio rewrite is nearly mechanical ONCE the underlying value is lifted, and cannot be done safely before it (e.g. `strlen(p)` can only become `s.len()` when `p` is a slice/str with a known length, not a bare `*const i8`). So children are split into (a) substrate lifting passes and (b) per-family call rewrites that depend on them.

Contrast with memchr: it is pointer-in/pointer-out, so it needed no type lift -- which is exactly why it was doable standalone. Most of this epic is not.

Correctness invariant (inherited from slate-04q): every idiomatization is a fixup; disabling it must still leave correct baseline Rust. Verify with differential tests + output-shape assertions.

## Context
Relates to the fixup epic slate-04q (shares the fixup module + correctness invariant). printf idiomatization is tracked separately as slate-04q.8; memchr as slate-04q.26 -- do not duplicate.
acceptance_criteria:
- A documented set of type-lifting substrate passes exists (string, slice, heap/handle), each usable independently.
- Per-family libc call-rewrite fixups are gated on the relevant substrate and are individually optional-in-spirit.
- Every rewrite is covered by a differential fixture and an output-shape assertion.
- docs/idiomatization.md describes the lift->rewrite dependency and the pointer-provenance / nul-termination invariants each pass relies on.
- Priority ordering reflects ease x commonality: common+mechanical rewrites land before rare or ownership-heavy ones.

title: Lower to a structured Rust AST instead of Item::Raw text
description:
Foundational cross-cutting change enabling all AST-based fixups. Do NOT wire hard bd blockers: this is done solo (no parallel agents) because it touches the whole lowerer.

Current state: the pipeline is already three-phase in shape (lower::lower -> Program, fixups::apply(Program) -> Program, Program::emit -> String; see main.rs:74-83), BUT lower.rs builds every function/global/record as Item::Raw(String) of pre-rendered Rust. So the 'AST' is a bag of strings: fixups munge text (src/fixups/mod.rs) and emit() just concatenates.

Goal: make lower() populate the REAL structured nodes already defined in src/rust_ast.rs (Func/Param/Block/Stmt/Expr/Type, with Raw escape hatches on Item and Expr). Then the three steps become meaningful: (1) build AST, (2) transform AST (fixups as Program->Program passes), (3) emit AST->string as the final step before writing files.

Scope of the migration:
- Expression layer: replace Val::Expr(String) with Val::Expr(rust_ast::Expr); build Binary/Unary/Cast/Compare/Call/Ref/Deref nodes instead of format! fragments. Use Expr::Raw as the bridge for constructs not yet modeled so the migration is incremental and stays byte-safe.
- Statement layer: replace self.out: String / emit_line(&str) with a Vec<Stmt>; let/assign/return/while/expr become Stmt nodes. Control-flow text stays via Stmt::Raw / new nodes as needed.
- Precedence-aware rendering: give Expr::render precedence context so redundant parens are simply never emitted (this delivers slate-04q.12 for free; baseline stays correct because extra parens are always safe).

Enables/precedes the AST-dependent fixups (reimplemented as AST passes, not text): slate-04q.12 (paren elision), slate-04q.11 (unnecessary mut), slate-04q.7 (arg temp inlining), slate-04q.3/.4/.5 (compound-assign / temp / retval cleanups). No hard deps recorded per instruction.

Verify: cargo nextest r --release stays fully green at every step (differential suite is the safety net); cargo fmt.
notes: touches: src/lower.rs (Val, materialize, emit_line, lower_func, expr constructors), src/rust_ast.rs (precedence rendering, Stmt::Raw), src/fixups/mod.rs (port to AST passes). Worktree: ../slate-04q.13
close_reason: Lowerer now builds structured rust_ast Expr/Stmt nodes (Val::Expr(Expr), Vec<IndentStmt> body, precedence-aware render). Merged to main. Remaining raw bridges tracked in slate-04q.15.

title: Record preprocessor conditional regions for cfg recovery
description:
Why: CIR and the normal Clang AST only contain the active preprocessed branch. To recover portable cfgs, Slate needs a preprocessing oracle that records conditional directives, predicates, source ranges, and whether each branch was active.

What to do:
- Extend the frontend path to collect #if/#ifdef/#ifndef/#elif/#else/#endif regions before CIR lowering.
- Preserve normalized predicate text and source ranges that can be joined to AST declarations and lowered Rust items.
- Track active versus inactive branches for the current invocation.
- Start with predicates used by tests/fixtures.cfg: _WIN32, __linux__, __APPLE__, architecture macros, and NDEBUG.

Out of scope: evaluating arbitrary project macro expressions beyond recording and simple known-predicate normalization.
acceptance_criteria:
Preprocessing metadata is available to later pipeline stages.
The cfg fixture predicates are recorded with source ranges and active/inactive state.
Unknown predicates are preserved as diagnostics/opaque expressions rather than guessed.
Existing single-config translation behavior is unchanged.
close_reason: Added preprocessing oracle (src/preprocess.rs) recording #if/#ifdef/#ifndef/#elif/#else/#endif regions with normalized predicates, directive/body source ranges, mapped Rust cfgs, and active/inactive state resolved against Clang's predefined macros. Unknown predicates are kept opaque + diagnosed, not guessed. Exposed via 'record-cfg' JSON command; recorded cfgs match tests/fixtures.cfg/expected_cfgs.json. Existing single-config/translate-cfg behavior unchanged. Verified with cargo nextest r --release (183 tests).

title: Run a bounded multi-config Clang/CIR matrix
description:
Why: disabled preprocessor branches cannot produce AST or CIR in a single Clang invocation. Slate needs a bounded multi-config mode that invokes the existing CIR pipeline for selected target/debug configurations.

What to do:
- Add a frontend mode that accepts or constructs a small configuration matrix.
- Include initial built-in configs covering Windows, Linux, Apple, x86_64, Arm/AArch64, debug, and NDEBUG-style release.
- Run each config through the existing emit-cir/parse/lower path and retain the predicate/config identity for each result.
- Cache or de-duplicate identical configs/results where practical.

Out of scope: exhaustive combinatorial exploration of arbitrary project macros.
acceptance_criteria:
The cfg fixtures can be translated under the relevant built-in or supplied configurations.
Each translated variant is tagged with the configuration/predicate that produced it.
Invalid or unsupported config variants fail with targeted diagnostics.
Existing single-config commands continue to work.
close_reason: Added experimental translate-cfg command with built-in OS, architecture, and NDEBUG macro config matrices. Variants run through existing CIR/AST/lower/fixup path, merge same-named whole functions for the fixture shape, and are verified by cfg fixture shape plus compile tests. Verified with cargo nextest r --release.

title: Merge whole-item cfg variants in the Rust emitter
description:
Why: after multiple config-specific CIR lowerings, Slate needs to stitch compatible Rust items into one portable Rust module guarded by cfg attributes. Whole items are the first tractable merge unit.

What to do:
- Identify matching source items across variants by source location, symbol name, and item kind.
- Emit #[cfg(...)] attributes for whole functions/globals/types when variants map cleanly to known Rust cfg predicates.
- Support alternate bodies for the same function name and cfg-exclusive items.
- Refuse expression-fragment or syntax-fragment macro cuts with diagnostics.

acceptance_criteria:

Conflicting variants that cannot be represented as whole Rust items are diagnosed.
Single-config output remains unchanged unless multi-config mode is selected.
close_reason: Rewrote translate-cfg to derive the whole-item cfg matrix from the lq0.2 preprocessing oracle instead of a filename table: each recorded branch -> a variant with clang args pinning every chain macro, rust_cfg from the recorded predicate mapping, validated against the oracle to activate exactly its branch. OS/arch/NDEBUG fixture output is unchanged. Refuses with diagnostics: fragment cuts inside a function/record body (brace-depth scan), predicates without a known cfg mapping, and >1 top-level chain (nested/sibling deferred). No-conditional sources pass through to single-config lowering (unchanged). Known limitation: negated/ifndef opening branches are validation-refused rather than merged (candidate uses a define-atoms heuristic); multi/nested chains deferred per epic scope. Added reject fixtures + tests. Verified cargo nextest r --release (195 tests) and cargo fmt.

title: Recover target/debug preprocessor configurations as Rust cfgs
description:
Why: Slate currently translates one preprocessed Clang/CIR view of a C file. Conditional compilation means untaken #if/#ifdef branches are absent from AST/CIR, so generated Rust is faithful only to the selected target/configuration, not to portable source that uses target/debug macro gates.

What to do:
- Add a multi-configuration frontend mode that records preprocessor conditional regions and runs Clang/CIR for a bounded set of meaningful configurations.
- Start with classic target/debug predicates: _WIN32, __linux__, __APPLE__, __x86_64__, __aarch64__/__arm__, and NDEBUG.

- Require user-supplied config sets for project-specific macro soup instead of guessing arbitrary combinations.
- Diagnose conditional regions that are not covered by any configured variant.

Out of scope initially: expression-fragment macro surgery, arbitrary combinatorial macro exploration, and translating inactive branches from a single Clang invocation.

title: Fuse local zero-init plus first assignment
description:
Why: baseline lowering initializes C locals to a zero value, then emits the first CIR store separately. In add.c this produces let mut c: i32 = 0; followed by c = ((a) + (b)); even though the first assignment can become the Rust initializer.

What to do:
- Recognize local declarations whose initializer is an artificial zero/default value and whose first read is preceded by exactly one dominating assignment.
- Rewrite let mut x: T = 0; ... x = expr; to let mut x: T = expr; when no read, address-take, volatile access, or aliasing-sensitive operation observes the placeholder value.
- Keep complex control flow, pointers, volatile locals, and address-taken locals on the baseline path until the analysis is explicit.
- This is the concrete dead-let/first-assignment cleanup exposed by add.c.
acceptance_criteria:
add.c generated Rust initializes c directly from a + b rather than zero-initializing and assigning separately.
Address-taken, volatile, and control-flow-ambiguous locals are left unchanged.
Differential tests stay green.
cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release pass.
close_reason: Added fuse_zero_init fixup: folds 'let mut x: T = 0; x = expr;' into 'let mut x: T = expr;' when the store is the immediately following line and does not read x. add.c now initializes c directly from a+b. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release (fixups unit tests + full differential suite green; cfg_translate failures are another agent's in-flight work in the coordination checkout, unrelated).

title: Collapse non-main retval boilerplate in fixups
description:
Why: helper functions currently lower C returns as __retval = value; return __retval;. Existing slate-04q.5 only covers main-specific store/load/process::exit cleanup, so ordinary function return boilerplate remains in fixtures such as add.c.

What to do:
- Recognize simple non-main patterns like __retval = expr; return __retval;.
- Rewrite to return expr; without changing control flow.
- Optionally fold final return expr; into a Rust tail expression only when it is the final statement in the function/block and type behavior is unchanged.
- Keep multiple-return and control-flow-heavy cases on the baseline path until proven.
- Add output-shape coverage using add.c or a focused return fixture.

Multiple-return and conditional-return fixtures continue to compile and behave correctly.
The fixup is optional in spirit; baseline lowering remains correct without it.
Differential tests stay green.

title: Recover simple printf calls as Rust format macros
description:
Why: generated Rust still emits unsafe extern printf calls for constant format strings such as printf("%d\n", add(2, 3)). That is correct baseline lowering, but it keeps unsafe/libc in the common easy case where Rust formatting can express the same output.

What to do:
- Recognize printf calls with a constant C string format argument.

- Preserve fallback to unsafe printf for dynamic formats, unsupported specifiers, locale-sensitive behavior, or ambiguous argument typing.
- Remove the now-unused printf extern declaration only when no printf calls remain.
- Add output-shape assertions and keep differential tests green.
acceptance_criteria:
add.c generated Rust uses println! for the three printf("%d\n", ...) calls.
Unsupported printf formats remain on the baseline unsafe extern path.
The printf extern declaration is removed when all printf uses are rewritten.
Differential tests stay green.

title: Eliminate parameter spill prologue in fixups
description:
Why: CIR faithfully spills every C parameter into an alloca + store because C params are mutable lvalues, so baseline lowering emits `let mut a: i32 = 0; ... a = arg0;` for each parameter. This is correct but noisy; the parameter binding can absorb the local directly.

What to do:
- Recognize, per parameter argK: exactly one local decl `let mut NAME: T = 0;`, exactly one store `NAME = argK;`, argK used nowhere else, and local type T equal to the param type.
- Rewrite the signature to bind the parameter under the local name, keeping mut (e.g. `fn add(mut a: i32, mut b: i32)`), and delete both the local decl and the spill store.
- Keeping mut in the signature preserves correctness when the C body reassigns the parameter. Address-of the parameter still refers to a real place.

Guards:
- Skip if NAME collides with another parameter name or another param renames to the same NAME.
- Skip if argK is used more than once (not a pure spill) or if the local type does not match the param type.
- This is a fixup: disabling it must still leave correct baseline Rust.

## Context
First of two fixups from add.c review. Low risk, independent of others, string-based rewrite is sufficient (type annotation just moves to the signature, no inference risk). Do this before the call-argument inlining fixup.
acceptance_criteria:
add.c generated Rust binds params under source names (fn add(mut a: i32, mut b: i32)) with no spill decls/stores.
Params reassigned in the C body still compile and behave correctly.
Address-taken parameters still work.
Differential tests stay green.
cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release pass.
close_reason: Implemented eliminate_param_spills fixup: folds the CIR parameter-spill prologue (let mut a=0; a=arg0;) into direct 'fn f(mut a: T, ...)' bindings when the slot is only seeded from its param and not read before the spill. String-based, keeps mut for later reassignment. Added 5 unit tests. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release (128 passed).

title: Improve stdlib test compilation performance
description: Stdlib coverage has grown large enough that test runtime is dominated by compiling many tiny generated Rust programs and matching C probes. tests/support::compare_batch already builds all generated Rust programs in one Cargo invocation under src/bin, but build_batch currently removes the whole batch project, including Cargo target artifacts, before every run. First investigate the minimal fix: preserve the batch Cargo target directory across runs and write generated/bin sources only when their contents actually change, so Cargo can reuse unchanged dependency and bin artifacts. If that is not enough, investigate a larger harness shape such as an aggregate Rust runner/module graph that dispatches per case. Preserve differential behavior, per-probe diagnostics, stdin/argv/env handling, stderr comparison, exit-code comparison, and fallback/error reporting for compile failures.
acceptance_criteria: stdlib_coverage repeat-run runtime is measurably reduced on the current corpus; unchanged generated Rust probes reuse Cargo artifacts where feasible; generated files are not rewritten unnecessarily; per-probe pass/fail output and known-unsupported ratchet behavior are preserved; harness comments explain cache invalidation and how to force a clean rebuild/debug an individual compile failure.
notes: Implemented local harness changes: preserve tests/support batch_cargo target artifacts, write generated/batch files only when bytes differ, and isolate KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED stdlib probes so expected compile failures do not force per-case fallback for all passing probes. Timing on this machine: clean target/stdlib-coverage cargo test --test stdlib_coverage -- --nocapture dropped from ~90s baseline to 21.32s real; immediate warm repeat was 17.90s real; cargo nextest r --release --test stdlib_coverage passed in 11.816s warm.

title: Recover compound assignment from CIR load-binop-store patterns
description:
Why: CIR lowers compound assignments like a -= 5 into load a, binop, store a. The Rust fixup should prefer compound assignment syntax when that pattern is safe, even though CIR alone cannot distinguish original a -= 5 from a = a - 5.

What to do:

title: Implement C goto lowering
description:
Why: C goto is currently unsupported even though ClangIR emits explicit cir.goto/cir.label/cir.br control-flow for it. translate also fails before lowering on successor lists such as [^bb2], so Slate cannot handle goto fixtures today.

What to do:

Right shift is arithmetic vs logical based on operand signedness, which Rust's >> already matches by type, so no extra work is needed there. Add a cir.shift arm in lower.rs that reads the isShiftleft attribute and emits Rust << or >>, add tests/fixtures/shl.c and shr.c fixtures, and extend tests/support/cgen.rs + c.bnf to emit shifts. - Transliterate single custom-macro #if chains to cfg(feature = ...), recovering both branches via the existing matrix.

description:
Why: translate-cfg refuses any conditional region whose predicate is not in known_cfg, including project flags like #ifdef MY_FEATURE. The faithful transliteration keeps BOTH branches and gates them with a Cargo feature, mirroring the C — not pinning the macro in single-config mode (which drops the inactive branch). defined(FOO) -> cfg(feature = "foo") is a syntactic 1:1 mapping, not a semantic guess: a build passing -DMY_FEATURE now passes --features my_feature.

What to do:
- Map custom (unmapped) atoms to feature cfgs: defined(FOO) -> cfg(feature = "foo") (normalized/lowercased); #ifndef -> not(...); boolean combos within a predicate compose via all()/any()/not() (just pred_to_cfg recursing).
- Handle MULTIPLE independent top-level chains via per-region attribution: pin only that chain's atoms, leave others at their default active branch, and gate just the items in that chain's line range. Independent regions do not multiply.
- Handle SOME nesting, bounded so codegen stays fast: allow nested #if up to a cap on generated configurations (e.g. a max nesting depth / max total variant count). Beyond the cap, refuse with a clear diagnostic pointing at the region rather than exploding into a 2^N matrix.
- Keep refusing value-carrying predicates (#if FOO == 2) and macros that reshape types (e.g. _FILE_OFFSET_BITS) rather than gate whole items.
- Document the -D -> --features correspondence and the nesting/variant cap in docs/cfg-portability.md.

Out of scope: unbounded nested/interacting macro exploration; guessing which feature combinations are meaningful.
design: Successor work under slate-mt9. Boolean and/any/not within a predicate is free (pred_to_cfg recursion). Multiple/nested chains need per-region attribution instead of the current global merge_variants (which keys items globally and forces a product). The nesting cap bounds the variant count so generation time stays bounded; pick the cap by generated-config count, not just depth.
acceptance_criteria: Custom single-macro chains translate both branches behind #[cfg(feature = ...)] / not(...); multiple independent top-level chains each gate their own region without a cross product; nesting is supported up to a documented bound (depth/variant cap) and refused beyond it with a region-pointing diagnostic; generated Rust compiles under the relevant feature states; value-macro and type-reshaping cases still refuse.
close_reason: Implemented project macro cfg(feature) mapping, per-region translate-cfg planning for multiple and nested whole-item chains with a 16-variant cap, docs, and cfg fixtures. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Extend known_cfg with obvious OS/arch/width macros
description:
Why: translate-cfg/record-cfg only map 7 predefined macros to Rust cfgs (src/preprocess.rs known_cfg). Several common target macros have unambiguous Rust equivalents but are reported as unmapped-macro today, so portable code that gates on them is needlessly refused. These are mechanical additions, not semantic guesses.

What to do:
- Extend known_cfg with the obvious target mappings, e.g.:
  - _WIN64 -> windows (or target_pointer_width = "64" + windows as appropriate)
  - __FreeBSD__ -> target_os = "freebsd"; __ANDROID__ -> target_os = "android"; __unix__ / other unixes as sensible
  - __i386__ -> target_arch = "x86"; __riscv -> target_arch = "riscv64"; __powerpc__/__wasm__ etc.
  - endianness/pointer-width: __LP64__/_LP64 -> target_pointer_width = "64"; endian macros -> target_endian
- Add each mapping to the docs/cfg-portability.md table (source of truth is known_cfg).
- Add cfg fixtures / expected_cfgs.json entries covering the new predicates.

Out of scope: compiler-identity macros (__GNUC__, _MSC_VER), value comparisons, and libc feature-test macros. Only add mappings where the Rust cfg is unambiguous.
design: Follow-up from the slate-lq0 preprocessor-cfg epic (now closed). Pure table extension in known_cfg; no changes to the merge/refusal machinery.
acceptance_criteria: New target macros map to their Rust cfg in record-cfg and translate-cfg; docs table updated; fixtures assert the mappings; ambiguous macros still report unmapped-macro.
close_reason: Implemented target macro mappings in src/preprocess.rs; updated cfg portability docs and record-cfg/translate-cfg fixtures for OS, arch, pointer-width, unix, win64, and ARM endian predicates. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Rewrite heap alloc: malloc/calloc/realloc/free to Box/Vec
description:
On lifted owned heap regions (slate-58r.3):
- malloc(sizeof(T))/single-object -> Box<T> (or MaybeUninit init)
- malloc(n*sizeof(T))/calloc -> Vec<T> / vec![init; n]
- realloc -> Vec::resize/reserve
- free -> drop (RAII); explicit free removed

Correctness hinges entirely on the ownership analysis in slate-58r.3: only single-owner, non-escaping regions convert. calloc's zero-init and realloc's move/grow semantics must be preserved.
acceptance_criteria: - Single-owner allocations render as Box/Vec with free replaced by scope-drop; calloc zeroes, realloc grows correctly.\n- Escaping/aliased/custom-allocator regions stay raw libc.\n- Differential fixtures cover alloc-fill-free and realloc-grow.

title: Rewrite numeric parse: atoi/atol/strtol/strtoul/strtod
description:
On lifted &str (slate-58r.1): atoi/atol/strtol/strtoul/strtod -> str::parse::<T>().

Semantic gap to handle carefully: C atoi returns 0 on failure and parses a leading numeric prefix; strtol reports the end pointer and errno on overflow. Rust parse() is all-or-nothing and returns Result. Preserve C's leading-prefix + default-0 behavior (e.g. trim/prefix-scan then unwrap_or(0)); do not silently change overflow/failure semantics.
acceptance_criteria: - Parses render via str::parse with C-equivalent failure/prefix semantics (leading-numeric prefix, default 0 for ato*).\n- strtol end-pointer/errno consumers keep correct behavior or stay raw.\n- Differential fixtures cover valid, leading-prefix, empty, and overflow inputs.
close_reason: Implemented lifted atoi/atol/strtol/strtoul/strtod rewrites through generated __slate_runtime parse support, preserving endptr strtol calls as raw. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Rewrite sort/search: qsort/bsearch to sort_by/binary_search
description:
On lifted &mut [T]/&[T] (slate-58r.2):
- qsort(base,n,sz,cmp) -> slice.sort_by(|a,b| <cmp>) (or sort_unstable_by)
- bsearch(key,base,n,sz,cmp) -> slice.binary_search_by(...)

Requires lifting the C comparator function pointer into a Rust closure returning Ordering, and the (base,n,sz) triple into a typed slice (element size must match T). Non-matching element size or opaque comparators stay raw.
acceptance_criteria: - qsort/bsearch over lifted slices render as sort_by/binary_search_by with a comparator closure returning Ordering.\n- Element-size mismatch or opaque comparator stays raw.\n- Differential fixtures cover sort-then-search on ints and structs.

title: Rewrite string search: strchr/strrchr/strstr/strpbrk/strspn/strcspn
description:
On lifted &str/&[u8] (slate-58r.1):
- strchr(s,c) -> s.find(c) (mapped back to a pointer/offset per the return contract)
- strrchr -> s.rfind(c)
- strstr(s,sub) -> s.find(sub)
- strpbrk -> s.find(|ch| set.contains(ch)); strspn/strcspn -> position of first (non)member

Return-contract care: C returns a pointer into the buffer (or NULL); the lift must map the found index back to the original pointer/offset, mirroring the memchr rewrite (slate-58r / slate-04q.26).
acceptance_criteria: - Searches render as find/rfind/position over lifted operands; NULL/None and pointer-offset mapping preserved.\n- Unlifted operands stay raw.\n- Differential fixtures cover hit, miss, and last-occurrence cases.
close_reason: Implemented lifted strchr/strrchr/strstr/strpbrk/strspn/strcspn rewrites with ASCII-aware string facts and byte-search fallback. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Rewrite string copy/concat: strcpy/strncpy/strcat/strncat
description:
On lifted String/&str targets (slate-58r.1):
- strcpy(d,s)/strncpy -> d = s.to_owned() / d.clear(); d.push_str(s)
- strcat(d,s)/strncat -> d.push_str(s)

Ownership-sensitive: destination must be an owned String or a bounded buffer; capacity/truncation semantics of the n-variants must be preserved. Unlifted or fixed-capacity buffers stay raw.
acceptance_criteria: - Owned-target copies/concats render as to_owned/push_str; bounded n-variants preserve truncation.\n- Unlifted targets stay raw.\n- Differential fixtures cover copy, append, and truncating-n cases.
close_reason: Implemented a string_copy AST fixup for safe local char buffers, rewriting unused strcpy/strncpy/strcat/strncat to String to_owned/push_str forms with truncating n-variant coverage. Verified with cargo fmt && cargo nextest r --release.

title: Substrate: lift (T*, len) pointer+length pairs to &[T] / Vec<T>
description:
Analysis + lowering pass that recognizes a raw `T*` together with an element count as a Rust slice (`&[T]`/`&mut [T]`) or owned `Vec<T>`. The count is in ELEMENTS, not bytes -- must not confuse with byte lengths from mem*/size arguments.

Unlocks qsort/bsearch -> sort_by/binary_search and typed memcmp -> slice ==. Requires proving the length correctly bounds the allocation and the region has valid provenance; otherwise keep raw pointers.

## Context
Gates slate-58r sort/search and typed-compare rewrites.
acceptance_criteria: - Recognized (ptr, len) pairs lower to &[T]/&mut [T]/Vec<T> with element (not byte) length.\n- Slice bounds provably within the backing allocation; unprovable cases stay raw.\n- Differential fixtures cover array params passed with a length and in-place mutation.
close_reason: Implemented ptr_len AST fixup for exact full-array (T*, len) calls, rewriting function params to slices and callers to as_slice/as_mut_slice while leaving partial or unproved lengths raw. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo test, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Substrate: lift heap and resource handles (malloc/free, FILE*) to owned Rust types
description:
Ownership-analysis pass that maps C heap allocations (`malloc`/`calloc`/`realloc`/`free`) to `Box<T>`/`Vec<T>`, and resource handles (`FILE*` from `fopen`, and similar) to owned Rust types (`std::fs::File` + `io`). Hardest substrate: requires tracking ownership/lifetime, single-free, and error paths so the RAII drop matches C's explicit free/close.

Where ownership can't be established (escaping pointers, custom allocators, double-free-prone flows), leave the raw libc calls in place.

## Context
Gates slate-58r heap and stdio rewrites. Highest risk; ordered last among substrates.
acceptance_criteria: - Provably single-owner heap regions lower to Box/Vec with Drop replacing free; escaping/ambiguous ones stay raw.\n- FILE* handles with clear open/close scope lower to std::fs::File; leaks/aliased handles stay raw.\n- Differential fixtures cover alloc-use-free and open-read-close round trips.
close_reason: Implemented scalar heap ownership facts and rewrite for provably single-owner malloc/free flows to Box<T>, with shared-walker guidance in AGENTS/CLAUDE. Verified with cargo nextest r --release.

title: Idiomatize __slate_memchr scan loop into .iter().position() fixup
acceptance_criteria:
- The generated `__slate_memchr` uses `.iter().position()` over a `slice::from_raw_parts` slice instead of a manual while-index loop.
- Pointer-return contract is preserved exactly: a match maps the found index back to `bytes.add(i) as *mut c_void`, and not-found returns `std::ptr::null_mut()` (same base pointer arithmetic as today, so a hit returns a pointer into the original buffer, not the slice copy).
- Fixup operates on rust_ast nodes, never rendered strings; disabling it still yields correct Rust (correctness invariant per epic).

title: Collapse declaration-initialized retval returns
description:
Why: generated helpers still emit patterns like 'let __retval: i32 = a & b; return __retval;' in bitand/div/mul/function_pointers and similar fixtures. This is correct but noisier than a direct return.

What to do:
- Add a fixup that recognizes a local __retval declaration with initializer immediately followed by 'return __retval'.
- Rewrite it to 'return <initializer>' and remove the declaration when __retval is not otherwise used.
- Keep multi-statement/multi-return retval cases on the baseline path.
- Preserve correctness if the initializer has side effects by only rewriting immediate declaration-return pairs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fixtures such as bitand.rs/function_pointers.rs no longer contain 'let __retval = ...; return __retval;' for simple helpers.
- Nontrivial retval control flow such as conditionals.classify remains unchanged unless separately proven.
- Differential tests stay green and output-shape coverage covers the direct return.

title: Collapse final return-only temps
description:
Why: many generated functions end with an immediate temp round trip such as 'let _v11 = values[2]; return _v11;' or 'let _v6 = unsafe { *slot }; return _v6;'. This survives current pure-temp inlining because some expressions are deliberately not considered movable.

What to do:
- Add a conservative fixup for the exact adjacent pattern 'let temp = expr; return temp'.
- Rewrite to 'return expr' when the temp is synthetic, not otherwise used, and the declaration is immediately before the return.
- Treat volatile reads and unsafe dereferences carefully; immediate replacement is acceptable only if evaluation count/order is unchanged.

Acceptance criteria:
- arrays.rs, pointers.rs, volatile.rs, and function_pointers.rs lose simple final return temp declarations where safe.
- Used temps and non-adjacent temps remain materialized.
- Differential tests and focused output-shape assertions pass.

title: Collapse simple main zero-exit retval tail
description:
Why: many generated main functions still end with '__retval = 0; let _vN = __retval; std::process::exit(_vN as i32);' because the current main retval fixup only handles the smallest round trip. This appears in compound_assignments, chars, pointers, atomics, and many more fixtures.

What to do:
- Recognize a final main tail that stores a constant zero into __retval, loads it into a temp, and exits with that temp.
- Rewrite the tail to 'std::process::exit(0 as i32)' when __retval is not needed for any later observable behavior.
- Do not remove earlier __retval scaffolding in functions with early exits, dispatch state, or nonzero exit paths unless separately proven.

Acceptance criteria:
- Representative fixtures no longer emit a final '_vN = __retval; std::process::exit(_vN as i32)' for constant-zero main tails.
- Nonzero and control-flow-sensitive exit behavior is preserved.
- Differential tests stay green.

title: Remove provably unnecessary parentheses in generated Rust
description:
rust_ast-level fixup that drops parentheses when Rust operator precedence and associativity make them provably redundant, so baseline lowering can keep emitting defensive parens for correctness while the fixup recovers idiom.

Baseline lowering wraps subexpressions in parens to preserve C evaluation order without reasoning about Rust precedence. Many are redundant once lowered (e.g. `(a * b) + c`, `return (x);`, `(a) + (b)`).

Scope: operate on the rust_ast, not text. Drop a paren group only when the parenthesized expression's precedence/associativity guarantees the same parse in its parent context; keep it otherwise. Must be precedence-correct across mixed arithmetic/bitwise/shift/comparison and unary contexts (Rust requires parens around some bitwise/comparison mixes — do not strip those).

Correctness invariant: this is an idiomatization fixup only. Disabling it must still yield correct Rust (extra parens are always safe). Pairs with slate-04q.7 (arg temp inlining) and slate-04q.11 (unnecessary mut removal), which also operate at the rust_ast layer.

title: Inline argument temps into type-safe call positions (rust_ast)
description:
Why: Baseline lowering materializes every call argument as its own let temp (e.g. `let _v1: i32 = 2; let _v3 = add(_v1, _v2);` then `printf(..., _v3)`). The existing pure-temp inliner (slate-04q.2) deliberately refuses call-argument positions because inlining a typed literal into a vararg slot loses its type (e.g. printf(_v0) with _v0: i64 = 9223372036854775807 must not become printf(9223372036854775807) — the literal would default to i32). Fixing this cleanly requires knowing callee signatures and preserving types, so this fixup should operate on the rust_ast, not on line-based text.

What to do:
- Move this fixup onto structured rust_ast nodes so callee signatures and argument types are available (per user direction: keep type information on the AST rather than a string side-table). The lowerer already emits every function signature; expose param types and the is_vararg flag to the fixup layer.
- Inline a single-use temp into a call-argument position when EITHER:
  (a) the callee is non-vararg and the target arg slot has a known param type (the param type pins any literal), OR
  (b) the temp initializer is itself a call (its return type is fixed by the callee signature, safe even in a vararg slot).
- Keep the existing hazard blocked: bare typed literals must NOT be inlined into vararg positions.
- For case (b) (impure call-result temp), require the def and use to be adjacent or separated only by pure temp-lets so no side effects are reordered.

Scope: only the two safe cases above. Do NOT emit `expr as T` casts to force a literal into a vararg slot — printf(2 as i32) is no cleaner than the temp and muddies the rule.

## Context
Second of two fixups from add.c review. User direction: handle on the rust_ast to keep type information (not a string side-table on the existing line rewriter). This is the "nontrivial fixup" the epic flagged as belonging on structured nodes. Depends on the parameter-spill fixup (slate-04q.6) landing first.

Typed literals are still NOT inlined into vararg positions (existing regression tests stay green).
Impure call-result inlining never reorders side effects.
Differential tests stay green.
cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release pass.
close_reason: Added call_args rust_ast fixup: inlines single-use temps into (a) declared param slots of non-variadic callees and (b) call-result temps into any slot (incl. vararg) when no side effect sits between def and use. title: Respect linkage when exporting cross-TU functions/globals as pub
description:
Why: translate-project currently emits every non-main function as 'pub fn' and every initialized global as 'pub static mut' (lower.rs, gated only on ProjectInfo.emit_pub). That is not linkage-accurate: a C file-scope 'static int x' / 'static void f()' has internal linkage and is private to its translation unit, but Slate exports it pub anyway. Today this is harmless (no sibling declares an internal-linkage symbol, so nothing imports it), but it leaks visibility and would misbehave if two units each defined a 'static' symbol of the same name that should stay distinct.

What to do:
- Read CIR linkage on cir.func / cir.global (internal vs external) and only emit 'pub' for external-linkage definitions; internal-linkage (C 'static') defs stay private (no 'pub').
- Correspondingly, do not enter internal-linkage symbols into the pass-1 defined/defined_globals maps, so a sibling never imports them.
- Add a fixture under tests/fixtures.multi exercising same-named 'static' symbols in two units plus an external shared one, proving they stay distinct and the external one still imports.

Acceptance:
- Internal-linkage (static) funcs/globals are NOT pub and NOT importable across modules.
- External-linkage symbols still export pub and import via 'use crate::<mod>::<sym>;'.
- Differential fixture passes; cargo fmt + cargo test pass.
design: CIR carries linkage on cir.func/cir.global (e.g. linkage=0 external vs internal, or sym_visibility=private). Determine the exact attr from emit-cir on a 'static' symbol, then gate emit_pub per-definition on it. Thread a small helper (linkage_is_external) rather than a bare emit_pub bool once per-symbol granularity is needed.
close_reason: Read CIR linkage on cir.func/cir.global; only external-linkage (linkage=0) defs emit pub and enter the pass-1 defined maps, so C statics stay module-private and unimportable. Added tests/fixtures.multi/static_linkage (same-named statics in two units + shared external). Verified: cargo fmt + cargo test (full suite green).

title: Derive Clone/Copy on emitted C structs and unions (value semantics)
description: C structs/unions are value types: assignment and pass-by-value copy them. Emitted #[repr(C)] structs derived nothing, so passing a struct by value and reusing it produced 'use of moved value' in Rust. Derive #[derive(Clone, Copy)] on all emitted records; every field type Slate emits (scalars, raw pointers, arrays-of-Copy, Option<fn>, LongDouble, nested records) is Copy, so the derive is always valid for the supported subset.

title: Escape C identifiers that collide with Rust keywords via raw identifiers (r#)

Four keywords cannot be raw identifiers (crate, self, super, Self) and must be mangled another way (trailing underscore).
design: Single choke point: sanitize_ident. After char-sanitizing, if the result is in the raw-unavailable set (crate/self/Self/super) append '_'; else if it is any other Rust keyword, prefix 'r#'. Raw idents are valid in type/field/fn/local positions so one fix covers all emit sites. union is a contextual keyword Slate itself emits for C unions — leave it usable as a plain ident.
close_reason: Implemented in src/lower.rs: LongDouble newtype (repr(C,align(16))) for long double, raw-identifier escaping for Rust-keyword collisions, and Clone/Copy derive on emitted C records. Full suite green incl. fuzzer; new fixture long_double_struct.c.

title: Represent long double as repr(C, align(16)) LongDouble newtype (layout fix)
description: Baseline long double currently lowers to bare f64 (8/8 layout), which silently breaks struct field offsets, union/memcpy punning, and array element placement wherever a long double shares a layout — the x86-64 SysV ABI wants size 16 / align 16. Introduce a #[repr(C, align(16))] struct LongDouble(f64) newtype with Add/Sub/Mul/Div/Neg impls so arithmetic still delegates to f64 (precision-lossy, tier 1) while the in-memory size/alignment matches the ABI. This is the layout tier; bit-exact x87 soft-float and libc/varargs interop remain out of scope (see slate-c2r).
design: Tier 1 of the long double ladder: correct layout, f64-precision arithmetic. rust_type maps !cir.long_double<...> to LongDouble; lower_const wraps literals as LongDouble(x); lower_cast converts int/float<->LongDouble via .0 / constructor; default is LongDouble(0.0). Prelude struct emitted only when used.
notes: DONE fully, including the C-AST struct-field path: c_type_to_rust(Float{bits:80}) -> LongDouble, default_c_value -> LongDouble(0.0), rust_c_type sets the prelude flag. Verified by tests/fixtures/long_double_struct.c (long double as struct field). Layout size=16/align=16 matches C on x86-64.
close_reason: Implemented in src/lower.rs: LongDouble newtype (repr(C,align(16))) for long double, raw-identifier escaping for Rust-keyword collisions, and Clone/Copy derive on emitted C records. Full suite green incl. fuzzer; new fixture long_double_struct.c.

title: Support ABI-exact long double libc interop

close_reason: Won't fix: ABI-exact long double varargs interop (%Lf) is unreachable in stable Rust — x86-64 SysV passes long double as class X87 on the stack, and Rust has no f80 type nor a way to classify a value as X87; LongDouble(f64) is a 16-byte INTEGER/MEMORY struct. Printing long double via %Lf is uncommon and the generator never exercises it (always truncates through %d). If needed later, the achievable path is format-in-Rust + %s rewrite (f64 precision), not varargs.

title: Value-carrying preprocessor predicates: rationale and bounded user-matrix path
description:
Why: numeric/value predicates like #if FOO == 2, #if FOO > 3, #if __GNUC__ >= 9 are refused (opaque-predicate) by translate-cfg. Root cause: Rust cfg / Cargo features are a BOOLEAN PRESENCE model — a feature is on or off and carries no value — so there is no cfg form for 'FOO's value >= 3'. This ticket captures the rationale and the only bounded, non-guessing path forward, distinct from the plain #ifdef work in slate-rs5.

Why it's hard (not just unimplemented):
- No direct mapping: cfg(feature=..) can't express a numeric comparison.
- Emulation requires enumerating the macro's VALUE DOMAIN into mutually-exclusive flags: FOO==2 -> cfg(feature="foo_2"); FOO>=2 -> cfg(any(feature="foo_2", feature="foo_3", ...)). C never states the domain, so inventing it is guessing project semantics (forbidden) and unbounded.
- Runtime lowering (const + if) does NOT rescue whole-item gating: both branches may define the same symbol differently, and two fn foo cannot coexist at runtime the way two #[cfg]-gated defs can.

Two sub-cases with different ceilings:
- Toolchain-fixed macros (__GNUC__, __STDC_VERSION__, _MSC_VER): value is concrete at translate time so the predicate is decidable, but Rust has NO compiler/language-version cfg, so there is no portable target — genuine dead end for portable recovery (only option is baking in the current toolchain's branch, which is unfaithful).
- Build-supplied value macros (-DVERSION=3): salvageable ONLY with a user-supplied value matrix -> mutually-exclusive feature encoding, with comparisons lowered to any()/all() over the enumerated set.

What to do:
- Document the boolean-presence limitation and these two sub-cases in docs/cfg-portability.md (why value predicates are refused).
- Design (not necessarily build) the user-supplied value-matrix interface: user declares FOO in {1,2,3}; Slate emits mutually-exclusive features and lowers ==, <, <=, >, >=, != to any()/all() over that domain, and enforces exactly-one-selected.
- Keep automatic (no-matrix) handling refusing with the opaque-predicate diagnostic.

Out of scope: guessing value domains automatically; compiler/language-version portability (no Rust cfg exists).
design: Successor under slate-mt9; the value-predicate counterpart to slate-rs5's boolean #ifdef work. Comparison lowering is any()/all() over an enumerated, user-declared domain with an exactly-one-of constraint. Toolchain-fixed version macros are explicitly not portably recoverable.
acceptance_criteria: Docs explain why value predicates are refused (boolean-presence cfg model) and the toolchain-fixed vs build-supplied split; a design exists for a user-supplied value matrix that lowers numeric comparisons to mutually-exclusive feature cfgs; without a matrix, value predicates still refuse via opaque-predicate diagnostics.
notes:
Value-matrix design (agreed spec):

Interface: user declares a per-macro BUILD VALUE SET (the values they actually compile with), e.g. LOG in {1, 1000000}. User declares VALUES, never features — Slate derives feature names and cfgs itself, best-effort.

Reduction (two composing passes):
1. Predicate partition: collect all distinct constants any comparison uses on the macro; sort into breakpoints; the value line splits into equivalence classes (each exact constant + open intervals between, clamped to domain) where every predicate has constant truth. Class count bounded by the CODE (<= 2k+1 for k constants), not the domain. Soundness rule: derive breakpoints from EVERY constant including == / != targets, so two values merge only when no predicate distinguishes them (then output is provably identical).
2. Build-set intersection: keep only classes containing a declared build value. Final feature cardinality <= number of declared values. This is the LOG in 1..1M -> 2 features collapse (e.g. {1}->A, {1000000}->D).

Lowering: emit one Cargo feature per surviving class, with an exactly-one-of constraint; each comparison -> cfg(any/all(...)) over the class features whose class satisfies it; &&/||/! compose as all/any/not.

In scope: each macro compared only to constants; boolean combinations of such comparisons, even across macros (LOG==2 && METRIC==3 -> all(feature=log_c2, feature=metric_c3)) since each atom is still single-macro-vs-constant.

Out of scope (refuse via opaque-predicate): CROSS-MACRO operands where a single comparison mixes two macros (LOG > METRIC, LOG + METRIC > 5) — needs the cartesian product of class sets, re-expanding cardinality. Decision: NO cross-macro combination declarations; one set per macro only. Affine arithmetic on a single macro (LOG*2 > 10 -> LOG > 5) is a possible later fold, not part of this.
close_reason: Closed

title: Rewrite stdio: fopen/fread/fwrite/fgets/fputs/fclose to std::fs + io
description:
On lifted FILE* handles (slate-58r.3):
- fopen -> std::fs::File::open/create (mode string -> OpenOptions)
- fread/fwrite -> Read::read/Write::write on the file
- fgets/fputs -> BufRead::read_line / write
- fclose -> drop (RAII)

Largest surface and lowest commonality in the current test corpus -> lowest priority. Buffering, error/errno, and EOF semantics must be preserved; stdin/stdout/stderr FILE* map to std::io::{stdin,stdout,stderr}.

title: Remove unnecessary unsafe around safe field reads
description:
Why: fixtures such as structs.rs and non_int_fields.rs emit 'unsafe { p.left }' for local struct field reads. Field access on safe local structs does not need unsafe, while union fields and static mut globals do.

What to do:
- Add a fixup or lowerer-side AST annotation that can distinguish safe struct field reads from union/static-mut field reads.
- Remove unsafe wrappers only for proven-safe local struct field accesses.
- Leave union field reads, static mut field reads, raw pointer derefs, and volatile accesses unsafe.

Acceptance criteria:
- structs.rs local Pair reads render as 'p.left'/'p.right' without unsafe.
- unions.rs and global_vars.rs keep required unsafe field/global access.
- Differential tests and output-shape assertions cover both removal and keep-safe cases.

title: Simplify constant array index casts
description:
Why: array fixtures emit indexes like 'values[(0 as usize)]' and globals emit 'numbers[(2 as usize)]'. These casts are correct but noisy for literal nonnegative indexes.

What to do:
- Add an expression fixup that rewrites literal integer index casts to plain usize-compatible literals in indexing positions.
- Start with nonnegative integer literals only: '0 as usize' -> '0'.
- Leave dynamic casts like '((index as i64) as usize)' alone unless a separate proof is added.

Acceptance criteria:
- arrays.rs/array_types.rs no longer contain '(0 as usize)' style indexes for literal constants.
- Dynamic and potentially signed indexes remain unchanged.
- Differential tests stay green.

title: Recover idiomatic pointer add/deref forms
description:
Why: pointer fixtures emit nested forms like 'unsafe { *unsafe { _v8.offset(_v9 as isize) } }' and copy fixtures embed 'unsafe { buf.as_mut_ptr().offset(...) }'. Rust exposes clearer raw-pointer APIs such as add/sub and can avoid nested unsafe blocks in some cases.

What to do:
- Analyze generated pointer arithmetic/deref AST shapes and choose a safer canonical spelling.
- Prefer nonnegative usize offsets with '.add(idx)' when the source index is known nonnegative; otherwise keep '.offset(...)'.
- Avoid changing aliasing, provenance, or signed-offset behavior.
- Collapse nested unsafe only when the inner/outer unsafe requirements are preserved.

Acceptance criteria:
- pointers.rs and mem_bcopy_overlap.rs have clearer pointer arithmetic spelling for proven-safe cases.
- Negative/signed offset cases remain baseline.
- Differential tests stay green with focused output-shape coverage.

title: Remove redundant one-statement block scopes
description:
Why: generated code still contains C-shaped scopes that only wrap a single structured statement, e.g. '{ if n < 10 { ... } }' in conditionals.rs and function_prototypes.rs. These scopes no longer add readability once control flow is structured.

What to do:
- Add a fixup that unwraps Stmt::Scope bodies containing exactly one structured statement and no declarations whose lifetime must be preserved.
- Start with singleton scopes around If/Match/Loop statements where removing the braces cannot change name visibility.
- Leave scopes that contain local declarations plus later statements, labeled blocks, or dispatch state machines unchanged until proven.

Acceptance criteria:
- conditionals.rs and function_prototypes.rs lose redundant outer braces around singleton if statements.
- Scope-sensitive fixtures still compile and behave correctly.
- Differential tests stay green.
